lamb-works-lucas-vol6:
Letters from 1821 to 1842 close Lucas's 1903 edition in this sixth volume. The contents open with a letter to Dorothy Wordsworth dated January 8, 1821. Soon after come notes to Thomas Allsop, Mrs. William Ayrton, Leigh Hunt, and Coleridge himself.

These were the years when the Elia essays made Charles Lamb famous. They were also years of growing sorrow, as old friends died and Mary's illness darkened the home. Charles died in 1834, yet the wit stays to the end. Read straight through, the letters form a tender, funny, and often sad record of a brother and sister's shared life together.
degroot-religious-system-china-vol6:
Volume Six, from 1910, completes de Groot's Religious System of China. The Dutch master's lifework closes with his summing of the whole. Six volumes survey one people's faith with unmatched breadth and depth.

De Groot draws his threads together on gods, souls, and rites. He restates how the dead, the spirits, and the priests interlock. His final judgments weigh China's faith as one vast, working whole. No Western scholar before or since matched the scope he achieved. The set stands as the fullest Western account of China's religious world ever made. Its close marks the end of a heroic age of field scholarship.
coke-reports-1777-vol6:
Wilson's 1777 edition of Coke's Reports nears its end with a sixth volume. Coke's decisions, gathered across a long career at the bar and on the bench, had grown into something close to a system. Wilson's Georgian edition put that system within reach of every practicing lawyer.

The cases continue the run of disputes over land, office, and the reach of the courts. Read in sequence, they show judge-made law building on itself, precedent by precedent. Coke's reports were never dry records; his prefaces and notes argue for the common law's wisdom against its rivals. Three centuries of lawyers have learned from these pages, and courts still cite Coke by name. The volume brings the reader close to the close of the greatest reporting career in English law.
